=== 2026-11-04 (59142) Letter re ERCOT Updates.docx ===


November 4, 2026


Public Utility Commission of Texas
Chairman Thomas J. Gleeson
Commissioner Kathleen Jackson
Commissioner Courtney K. Hjaltman
Commissioner Morgan Johnson
Commissioner Patrick Rhode

1701 N. Congress Avenue
Austin, TX 78711

Re:	PUC Project No. 59142, Review of ERCOT’s Interconnection Processes for Large Loads – ERCOT Updates: Batch Zero Verification and Audit Process, Data Center State and Community Impact RFI, and Medium Load RFI 
Dear Chairman and Commissioners: 
	Attached are three presentations that provide updates on several important initiatives relating to the interconnection of Large or Medium Loads in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc. (ERCOT) Region.  Attachment A provides a status update on ERCOT’s ongoing Batch Zero verification and audit process, including an update on some of the most common verification issues ERCOT has identified in this process to date.  Attachment B provides some initial information about the responses ERCOT has received in response to its Data Center State and Community Impact Request for Information (RFI), including some information on the size, function, and location of data centers based on submitted information.  Finally, Attachment C provides an update on an RFI ERCOT has recently issued to Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) and Distribution Service Providers (DSPs) to obtain additional information about Medium Loads (less than 75 MW) that have requested interconnection in the ERCOT Region.  I will be prepared to discuss these with you at the November 5, 2026 open meeting.
	Also, please note that ERCOT is continuing its evaluation of requests for potential good cause exceptions relating to the Batch Zero eligibility criteria in Planning Guide Revision Request (PGRR) 145 that were submitted in response to ERCOT’s July 23, 2026 Market Notice.  As discussed at the Commission’s August 20, 2026 open meeting, ERCOT has determined that the only developer-submitted good cause exception requests it intends to pursue are those that sought additional time to post financial security beyond the deadline established in PGRR145 and those that requested additional time to submit a late Form W, regarding Provisional Controllable Load Resource (PCLR) status.  With respect to the first of these two requests, ERCOT has confirmed that each of the Large Loads seeking a later security posting deadline has now posted that security; granting the exception would simply recognize that late posting as sufficient to meet the PGRR145 eligibility criteria.  
ERCOT also intends to seek a good cause exception on its own initiative outside of the process defined in the Market Notice.  This additional exception concerns Large Loads that were submitted as energized loads under Planning Guide Section 9.2.1.1(1)(b), but that ERCOT determined had not energized by July 10, 2026.  ERCOT intends to ask the Commission to allow those loads to submit eligibility materials after the deadline so they may qualify under Section 9.2.1.1(1)(e).  ERCOT expects to file these good cause exception requests for PUC consideration next week, which would allow the Commission to consider them at the December 17, 2026 open meeting.  
Respectfully,

 /s/ Chad V. Seely		
Chad V. Seely
SVP, Regulatory Policy, General Counsel, and Chief Compliance Officer
chad.seely@ercot.com

 PUBLIC         Executive Summary
     PRELIMINARY AS OF 11/5, SUBJECT TO CHANGE



         •    ERCOT issued the Data Center State and Community Impact Request for Information (RFI) to 465 loads.
         •    433 of 465 loads (93%) submitted the RFI, covering ~177 GW (~97%) of requested interconnection capacity.
              – 417 RFIs were submitted on time (most due 5pm CT on 10/12), and 16 were submitted late. 32 Medium Load
                responses have not been submitted.
              – All 245 Large Loads (75 MW or greater) responded to the RFI.
              – Large Loads represent ~94% of requested interconnection capacity (~166 GW). Among Large Loads, 33 projects
                representing 36% of capacity are requesting interconnections greater than 1 GW.
              – Requests span every ERCOT Load Zone; West Texas represents the plurality with 41% of capacity (73 GW).
             • Respondents answered 83% of the nearly 67,000 RFI questions, sufficient to provide a statistically meaningful
               analysis for the final report.
              – Projects with later planned energization dates (e.g., 2028+) had a higher rate of “Not Applicable or unable to
                answer” (‘N/A’) responses, commensurate with lower project maturity.
              – Medium Loads with energization dates planned pre-2028 included 'N/A' responses at a higher rate than Large
                Loads, indicating developers had not decided on some critical equipment configurations (e.g., cooling technology).
         •    Detailed data analysis is currently underway, and ERCOT is targeting a published final report on December 10, 2026.

                 Dear Chairman and Commissioners:
                         Attached are three presentations that provide updates on several important initiatives
                 relating to the interconnection of Large or Medium Loads in the Electric Reliability Council of
                 Texas, Inc. (ERCOT) Region. Attachment A provides a status update on ERCOT's ongoing Batch

                 issues ERCOT has identified in this process to date. Attachment B provides some initial
                 information about the responses ERCOT has received in response to its Data Center State and
                 Community Impact Request for Information (RFI), including some information on the size,
                 function, and location of data centers based on submitted information. Finally, Attachment C

                 (TSPs) and Distribution Service Providers (DSPs) to obtain additional information about Medium
                 Loads (less than 75 MW) that have requested interconnection in the ERCOT Region. I will be
                 prepared to discuss these with you at the November 5,2026 open meeting.
                        Also, please note that ERCOT is continuing its evaluation of requests for potential good
                 cause exceptions relating to the Batch Zero eligibility criteria in Planning Guide Revision Request
                 (PGRR) 145 that were submitted in response to ERCOT's July 23, 2026 Market Notice. As
                 discussed at the Commission' s August 20,2026 open meeting, ERCOT has determined that the
                 only developer-submitted good cause exception requests it intends to pursue are those that sought
                 additional time to post financial security beyond the deadline established in PGRR145 and those
                 that requested additional time to submit a late Form W, regarding Provisional Controllable Load
                 Resource (PCLR) status. With respect to the first of these two requests, ERCOT has confirmed
                 that each ofthe Large Loads seeking a later security posting deadline has now posted that security;
                 granting the exception would simply recognize that late posting as sufficient to meet the PGRR145
                 eligibility criteria.
                        ERCOT also intends to seek a good cause exception on its own initiative outside of the
                 process defined in the Market Notice. This additional exception concerns Large Loads that were
 submitted as energized loads under Planning Guide Section 9.2.1.1(1)(b), but that ERCOT
determined had not energized by July 10, 2026. ERCOT intends to ask the Commission to allow
those loads to submit eligibility materials after the deadline so they may qualify under Section

meeting.

            PRELIMINARY AS OF 11/5, SUBJECT TO CHANGE



                 ·    ERCOT issued the Data Center State and Community Impact Request for Information (RFI) to 465 loads.
                 ·   433 of 465 loads (93%) submitted the RFI, covering -177 GW (-97%) of requested interconnection capacity.
                     - 417 RFIs were submitted on time (most due 5pm CT on 10/12), and 16 were submitted late. 32 Medium Load
                         responses have not been submitted.
                     - All 245 Large Loads (75 MW or greater) responded to the RFI.
                     - Large Loads represent -94% of requested interconnection capacity (-166 GW). Among Large Loads, 33 projects
                       representing 36% of capacity are requesting interconnections greater than 1 GV\L
                     - Requests span every ERCOT Load Zone; V\/est Texas represents the plurality with 41% of capacity (73 GW).
                     · Respondents answered 83% of the nearly 67,000 RFI questions, sufficient to provide a statistically meaningful
                      analysis for the final report.
                     - Projects with later planned energization dates (e.g., 2028+) had a higher rate of "Not Applicable or unable to
                       answer" ('N/A) responses, commensurate with lower project maturity.
                     - Medium Loads with energization dates planned pre-2028 included 'N/A' responses at a higher rate than Large
                       Loads, indicating developers had not decided on some critical equipment configurations (e.g., cooling technology).
                 ·    Detailed data analysis is currently underway, and ERCOT is targeting a published final report on December 10, 2026.
